title: Capability inventory
summary: Check what your organization can actually run before choosing the architecture.

sections.label: Inventory
items: The clients, extensions, runtime and versions actually used.
Models available under the applicable account and organization settings, where AI is used.
The model actually reported for each role or delegated run, when relevant.
Supported tools and integrations, their permissions and the identity performing each action.
Access to the relevant source, checks, data and execution environment.
Operating ownership, billing, budgets and evidence retention.

sections.label: Example inventory
sections.text: For the workplace example, inspect Copilot in IntelliJ, Rovo connections, and access to Bitbucket, Jenkins and Neptune. Another project needs an inventory of its own systems.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Every proposed integration has a tested execution path. A feature announced for one client is not treated as available in every client.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow steps: Understand the current process, Define the proposed outcome, Architecture and impact. These links are recommendations based on the guide content, not required product or process choices.
An inventory names the client, plugin, runtime and integration versions, with the source used to confirm each.
For each proposed action, a capability matrix records the actor, access boundary and an observed bounded probe, or explicitly marks the path untested.
The design decision references only demonstrated capabilities and names an owner for each unresolved dependency or billing boundary.
Existing source claims were not re-audited in this mapping pass. Project configuration, usefulness and actual check outcomes remain unverified.

catalog.applicability: Use this before choosing an architecture or proposing an integration, to record which clients, models, tools, access and budgets your organization can actually run. A feature announced for one client counts as available only where its execution path has been tested.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
